answers.answer: Each player takes 12 ordinary turns. A courtship is only an event: no player turns, service rotation, monument income, or Servants’ Hall use.
answers.evidence: Overview; Round-track events: ‘each player takes twelve ordinary turns’ and ‘no ordinary turn or ongoing income.’

answers.answer: Hosting order: rotate service (Quarters to Available, then Expended to Quarters); resolve the round event; resolve applicable monument and Servants’ Hall effects; choose an activity tile; invite the exact required gentry; provide required services; resolve all positive favours before negative favours; optionally buy one tile; then send all used servants to Expended Service, played gentry to personal discard, and return the tile to its tableau column, flipping/upgrading if required. The last player advances the round marker.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Hosting an activity; Player Reference → Host.

answers.answer: Pass order: all servants directly to Available Service; all gentry in personal discard to hand; round event then ongoing tile effects; choose £200 or one free Market refresh; optionally buy one tile; last player advances the marker. If a servant was used for an ongoing effect, it goes to Expended Service at turn end. Butler’s Room hiring is an activity, not a pass benefit.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Passing; the stated ordered sequence.

answers.answer: Yes. Screening is fixed at the end of step 2, so 6.1 qualifies the PR6 activity and guests for the whole activity even after Service Help lowers current reputation to 3.4. Each Service Help costs 3 increments and moves one servant from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service; it cannot take one directly from Expended Service. Four uses cost 12 increments.
answers.evidence: Actions → Reputation, wealth and special actions; screening is fixed before Choose Activity; Service Help table row.

answers.answer: Resolve all positive favours before all negative favours; the order within each group is up to the player. At minimum reputation, a negative reputation favour cannot reduce reputation below 1.1, but you cannot take a negative favour first to avoid paying a loss. A money penalty must be paid in full; positive activity money favours, a money VP card, or Borrow Money may fund it. If you cannot fund it, you cannot play that guest/tile.
answers.evidence: Hosting an activity → Enjoy favours; Actions → money penalty; Special Rules & Edge Cases.

answers.answer: Borrow Money: lose 2 reputation increments, gain £100; repeatable. Service Help: lose 3 increments, move one servant from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service; repeatable. Refresh Market: lose 4 increments and fully refresh; once per turn. No special action is allowed at minimum reputation. Service Help cannot move a servant straight from Expended Service.
answers.evidence: Actions → Reputation, wealth and special actions, special actions table.

answers.answer: Host the Butler’s Room Servant Hiring activity using an available butler or underbutler and no gentry. Take up to two non-underbutler servants from Servants for Hire into Expended Service; there is no hiring fee. On first use the tile upgrades at cleanup. The upgraded room may instead recruit one common footman, valet, or lady’s maid from any location on one opponent’s family board into your Expended Service; unique servants cannot be recruited.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring → Butler’s Room.

answers.answer: A housekeeper substitutes for a lady’s maid only when no lady’s maids are available. With Brushing Room in your tableau, footmen substitute for valets only when no valets are available. An underbutler may substitute for a butler, valet, or footman even if that type is still available.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring; substitution rules.

answers.answer: Acquire an underbutler only by purchasing Butler’s Pantry; it goes immediately into Expended Service. Normally it reaches Servants’ Quarters at the next service rotation and Available Service at the second subsequent rotation; passing or a Refresh Service VP card can accelerate availability, and once in Quarters Service Help or the Servants’ Quarters tile can allow earlier use. Another player cannot recruit it because it is unique, not common.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring → Butler’s Pantry.

answers.answer: Market price is the space price plus the tile’s printed modifier. Reserve base price is £300 plus the modifier. Price cannot be below £100. You may not acquire a duplicate tile already owned. Reputation does not restrict buying, so a tile above your reputation may be bought.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve → Normally buy one tile total.

answers.answer: If a Market space empties, slide remaining tiles left and draw replacements into the rightmost spaces. A drawn duplicate stacks on the matching Market tile and another tile is drawn. A tile qualifying for Reserve goes directly to Reserve and another is drawn. If filling multiple spaces, sort only newly drawn tiles by sorting number. Buying one tile from a two-tile stack leaves the space occupied and does not trigger refill.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve → Refill.

answers.answer: After courtship 1, move all Market Service tiles except Largest Wine Cellar to Reserve; later drawn Service tiles go straight there except Largest Wine Cellar. After courtship 2, also move all Market PR1 tiles to Reserve, and send later PR1 draws directly there. Largest Wine Cellar never enters Reserve. The Market is fully refreshed after each of the first three courtships as standard in this source, after Reserve movement.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve → Open Reserve and Refresh; Overview scope.

answers.answer: At each courtship, return both Fairchilds to Alderley Hall first. For courtships 1–3, score tile VP for the current theme, including negative VP; only the currently face-up hybrid category counts. Highest score gets one VP card and chooses one Fairchild. A tie means each tied player draws one VP card and nobody gets a Fairchild. Each player discards one objective; shuffle simultaneous discards together and bottom-deck them. Seasonal upkeep: open the relevant Reserve, fully refresh the Market, reveal the next theme to the right of prior themes, pass first player anticlockwise, advance the round marker.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Courtship and seasonal upkeep.

answers.answer: Final courtship scores tile VP for all four revealed themes; repeated categories count each time, including negative values. Highest gets one VP card and a Fairchild; on a tie, highest reputation level breaks it, ignoring wheel position. If still tied, no Fairchild is awarded and tied winners draw VP cards under the courtship tie rule. Discard the final objective, then players get a final chance to use special actions and VP card benefits where possible before moving the marker to Wedding Bells and scoring.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Final courtship (round 16).

answers.answer: End-game VP comes from face-up printed VP on all improvement tiles (including negatives); gentry VP in hand and discard (including negatives, family, final Fairchild); fulfilled objectives; reputation level 1–7 worth 1/3/6/10/15/21/28 VP; 2 VP per servant of any type/location; 1 VP per £200 rounded down; and printed VP on retained unused VP cards. Ties: final Fairchild holder wins; otherwise highest reputation level; if still tied, share victory.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Final VP.

answers.answer: Normally each player starts with five objectives, draws two at round 6, and discards one at each of four courtships, retaining three to score. Additional objectives from Main Library or a VP card add to the final retained count and do not trigger an extra discard. Simultaneous discards are shuffled together, then placed face down on the bottom of the objective deck. Tile objectives require owning the named tile at game end, not upgrading it.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards.

answers.answer: A VP card’s benefit may be used immediately when drawn, at any time on a later own turn (multiple cards allowed), and once more after final courtship before scoring. Used cards go to the bottom of the VP deck. Retained cards remain hidden with objectives and score their printed VP; a card cannot provide both benefit and final VP.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards.

answers.answer: A normal activity tile must flip to its rose/upgrade side after first use; an already-upgraded normal tile remains upgraded on later uses. Hybrids start with the underlined category icon, flip after every use, and the newly face-up category counts for courtship and objectives. A Queen’s or Lionheart Suite upgrades into a monument after its single activity use and can never host again; its ongoing benefit starts on later turns.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects; suite activity table.

answers.answer: Monuments and Servants’ Hall resolve during ongoing effects: step 2 on hosting and step 3 on passing, after the event; courtship has no ongoing income/use. Monuments give one reputation each per ordinary turn. Servants’ Hall uses one available servant to lower one opponent’s reputation by one and raise yours by one; that servant cannot serve the activity and goes to Expended Service at turn end. Do not target a player at minimum reputation.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure; Improvements and ongoing effects → Monuments and Servants’ Hall.

answers.answer: Heritage Guest Suite uses one footman on the tile and one casual guest from hand, with the guest’s normal service; it doubles all that guest’s favours, including negative ones, and upgrades into an activity tile. Queen’s Suite uses a housekeeper and one prestige guest from hand with normal guest service; double one chosen favour and resolve others normally; it upgrades into a monument. Lionheart Suite uses a butler and draws one prestige guest to attend, needing no personal guest service; double nonnegative favours, not negative ones, and keep the guest in discard at cleanup; it upgrades into a monument. Each has a fixed one-guest count that cannot be changed.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects → Suite activity table and fixed-count note.

answers.answer: Choose a random first player and give them the first-player marker. Starting with the player to that player’s left and proceeding clockwise, players choose an available base family. Bonuses: Asquith adds its Dowager Countess as a fifth family card; Cavendish starts at reputation 1.4; Ponsonby gains £300; York adds a footman to Available Service.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1 and 5.

answers.answer: Each player gets reputation level 1, position 1 and the 1/2, 3/4, 5/6 and Max counters stacked with 1 showing (no 7/8 counter). They receive one butler, housekeeper, valet, lady’s maid and footman in Available Service; five starter tiles (Private Study, Butler’s Room, Main Gazebo, Front Parlour, Bowling Green) with starter/building icon showing; and Lord, Lady, Heir, Young Lady family cards. Only Ponsonby starts with money (£300); Cavendish has the reputation bonus, and Asquith/York their other bonuses.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 2, 3 and 5.

answers.answer: For three players put three valets, three lady’s maids, six footmen, and two underbutlers in Servants for Hire. No butlers or housekeepers are stocked. Unused servants return to the box and are unavailable this game.
answers.evidence: Setup step 6.

answers.answer: Separate starter guests from the casual deck, shuffle the starter guests, and deal two to each player. Shuffle every undealt starter back into the casual deck. Starter guests are casual guests with a starter icon and otherwise follow normal casual rules.
answers.evidence: Setup step 4; Gentry, screening, dismissal and family.

answers.answer: For four players select five double-sided monuments (one per player plus one), choosing at most one of Sculpture Garden and Garden Maze. Tiles that later upgrade into monuments are all placed in the bag and do not count toward the five selected double-sided monuments.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7.

answers.answer: Opening Market has six different eligible tiles: PR3 or lower (including no PR), excluding Servants’ Hall and double-sided monuments. Set ineligible draws aside and return them to the bag after filling; stack duplicate eligible draws in the matching space. Normal tiles enter with the upgrade/rose icon hidden; hybrids with the underlined hybrid icon showing. Sort six spaces by ascending sorting number, starting at the £300 space. PR4 tiles, Servants’ Hall, and double-sided monuments are ineligible.
answers.evidence: Setup step 8.

answers.answer: Put Alderley Hall standard side up, round marker at 1, and one reminder token per player above the track. Shuffle theme and VP decks separately; reveal the first theme for open courtship. Keep revealed themes in order through the game, so old revealed themes remain. Place base Charles and Elizabeth Fairchild face up on Alderley Hall. The first theme is not hidden.
answers.evidence: Setup step 9.

answers.answer: At hosting-turn service rotation, a servant in Servants’ Quarters moves to Available Service, while a servant in Expended Service moves to Servants’ Quarters. An unused Available Service servant remains available; it does not move.
answers.evidence: Hosting an activity, step 1: Rotate service.

answers.answer: No. Village Fair event is resolved before choosing the activity, and the Private Study must already be upgraded at that step. An upgraded Study gives £300 and 2 reputation. Village Fair occurs on standard spaces 3 and 9.
answers.evidence: Round-track events table; Private Study description.

answers.answer: On standard space 6, resolve Draw Objectives during each player’s turn after service rotation and before ongoing effects/choosing an activity (or during the equivalent event step when passing). Draw two and keep both secret with other objectives. Passing players receive the event too.
answers.evidence: Hosting/pass order; Round-track events table: Draw two objectives; event applies on each player’s turn.

answers.answer: Yes. National Holiday waives PR on all tiles and guests when hosting. All other requirements remain, including service and exact gentry counts/types.
answers.evidence: Round-track events table; National Holiday.

answers.answer: Yes, Builders’ Holiday permits any number of Market and/or Reserve purchases within funds, at the current prices. Finish all purchases before sliding/refilling; use one unchanged market and do not refresh between purchases, including by special action or VP card. Market Purchase VP cards follow the same single-unchanged-market rule; they can allow multiple purchases under that rule.
answers.evidence: Round-track events; Builders’ Holiday / Market Purchase VP card.

answers.answer: Set all Market tiles aside and leave Reserve unchanged. Refill all six Market spaces under normal rules, sorting as required; only after refill return the set-aside tiles to the bag and mix them in. Thus removed tiles cannot reappear in that same refresh. Reserve tiles are unaffected.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve → Refresh.

answers.answer: Each reputation symbol is one increment. Crossing position 5 to 1 raises the level; crossing 1 to 5 lowers it. The standard minimum is 1.1 and maximum 7.5 (Max.5); losses beyond minimum are ignored. At Max.5, excess gains are lost unless immediately spent on special actions; special actions can be taken before or during a reputation favour to create room.
answers.evidence: Actions → Reputation, wealth and special actions.

answers.answer: Money is public. Players cannot give or receive money between them. Never spend more than you hold. The supply is unlimited; use proxies if needed.
answers.evidence: Actions → Reputation, wealth and special actions, money paragraph.

answers.answer: Family members may fill ladies or gentlemen requirements according to gender. They cannot fill casual-guest requirements, which require guests of that type and exclude family. Exact attendee number and types are mandatory; no extra gentry may be played. Family has no PR and needs no personal service.
answers.evidence: Hosting an activity → Invite gentry; screening rules.

answers.answer: For screening draws, draw the stated number, choose the stated number to keep, reveal only kept cards, and add kept cards to hand; put rejected cards on the bottom of their deck without revealing them. The general guest-invite favour draws from the indicated deck, reveals the guest to everyone, and adds it to hand.
answers.evidence: Gentry, screening, dismissal and family; Hosting an activity → Enjoy favours.

answers.answer: Dismissal is always optional, so with no unwanted guests you need not dismiss. You may dismiss an eligible guest from hand, current activity, or discard, including a guest drawn earlier during Enjoy Favours. Family cannot be dismissed. Put the guest on the bottom of its matching deck; it is no longer yours, will not return on passing, and does not score for you.
answers.evidence: Gentry, screening, dismissal and family → Dismissal.

answers.answer: Lord: £200. Lady: choose screening two casual guests and keeping one, or optionally dismiss one guest. Heir: choose £100 or one reputation. Young Lady: draw one casual guest. Asquith Dowager: both £100 and one reputation. Thus Lady and Heir choose; Dowager gets both, and Lord/Young Lady each give their stated benefit.
answers.evidence: Base family card table.

answers.answer: She gets the admirer bonus only when a male prestige guest attends the same activity. The bonus is two reputation. She still draws one casual guest. A male casual guest or female prestige guest does not satisfy the bonus; Charles Fairchild does, because he is a male prestige guest.
answers.evidence: Base family card table; Fairchild gender/type paragraph.

answers.answer: Charles is a male prestige guest with no PR, requires a valet, and gives three reputation. Elizabeth is a female prestige guest with no PR, requires a lady’s maid, and gives both one prestige guest and two reputation. Fairchilds behave as prestige guests, not family, and so are not covered by family’s dismissal immunity.
answers.evidence: Gentry, screening, dismissal and family; Charles and Elizabeth paragraph.

answers.answer: Miss Elizabeth Perkins reduces one opponent’s reputation by one. Miss Florence Oliver reduces one opponent by two and makes you lose one reputation. Minimum-reputation protection means a player at 1.1 cannot be targeted by an opponent’s reputation-reducing effect.
answers.evidence: Base family card table section’s gossip paragraph; reputation minimum rule.

answers.answer: A Barn gives one reputation each time you host an Estate activity. Merely owning an Estate tile or passing earns none.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects → Barn.

answers.answer: Servants’ Quarters tile lets you use one servant from the Servants’ Quarters area each turn in addition to Available Service; that servant goes to Expended Service after use. Service Help instead costs 3 reputation and moves one Quarters servant to Available Service. Ordinary hosting rotation moves Quarters to Available and Expended to Quarters; these are separate mechanisms.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring → Servants’ Quarters tile; Service Help; Turn Structure rotation.

answers.answer: Private Study’s front activity requires two family and a butler; it has no tile favour. It upgrades permanently into an ongoing tile, and its upgraded side gives £300 and two reputation only on Village Fair rounds. You cannot repeatedly host it after upgrading because the upgraded tile is ongoing and cannot host an activity.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects → Private Study.

answers.answer: Unupgraded Main Library requires a butler and two family and draws one extra objective. Upgraded Main Library requires a butler and three family and draws one VP card. The extra objective increases the objectives retained for final scoring; it does not trigger an extra courtship discard.
answers.evidence: Main Library paragraph; Objectives and VP cards.

answers.answer: Objective VP card: draw two objectives, keep one, and return the other to the bottom of the objective deck. It provides one additional retained objective for final scoring.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table → Objective.

answers.answer: Yes. Refresh Service moves all servants directly to Available Service, usable immediately, including servants from Expended Service. Service Help only moves one servant from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service and cannot take one straight from Expended Service.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table → Refresh Service; special action table → Service Help.

answers.answer: Hire Servant takes one servant from Servants for Hire, excluding underbutlers, into Expended Service. It cannot provide service immediately from there; normal availability requires later movement, though the summary gives no special immediate exception for Hire Servant.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table → Hire Servant; Servants and hiring rotation rules.

answers.answer: No. Refresh Guest returns one gentry from your personal discard to hand. A family member in discard can be returned; it is not drawn from the current activity, and because it is in hand rather than played, that card cannot attend this activity.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table → Refresh Guest; played cards are in personal discard and activity attendees are played from hand.

answers.answer: The basic-servant objective counts only common footmen, valets, and lady’s maids; it excludes butler, housekeeper, and underbutler. Normal servant VP counts every servant, all types and locations, at 2 VP each. The ten-servant objective gives 7 VP for at least ten servants total.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference → Basic servants; Final VP → Servants.

answers.answer: The upgraded Queen’s Suite and Lionheart Suite count as monuments for the monument objective, worth 3 VP each. Category objectives count monuments and hybrids according to their currently face-up category; hybrids count only as the face-up category.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference → Monuments and category bonuses; Improvements and ongoing effects → Hybrids.

answers.answer: Nature Group is 11 VP for Flower Room plus one of English Garden, French Garden, Sculpture Garden, or Garden Maze. Domestic Group is 12 VP for Gabled Conservatory plus either Main Library or North Library. Tiles need only be owned at game end; use is not required.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference; tile objectives need owning, not upgrading/using.

answers.answer: Prestige-guest objective awards 1 VP per prestige guest. Every-three-guests objective awards 1 VP per complete group of three nonfamily guests; an incomplete group earns no point. A final Fairchild is a prestige guest and counts for the prestige-guest objective; as nonfamily gentry it also counts among guests for groups of three.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference → Guest bonuses; Fairchilds and final scoring sections.

answers.answer: The reputation objective earns 7 VP for reaching maximum reputation level 7, regardless of wheel position. The wealth objective earns 10 VP for at least £1200. Ordinary reputation VP is based on level only, not wheel position; reputation wheel position also does not break reputation ties.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference → Reputation and Wealth; Final VP reputation and tie rules.

answers.answer: Both sides of West Terrace require one butler and exactly three family cards. Unupgraded side favours: draw one prestige guest. Upgraded side: draw one prestige guest and optionally dismiss one to four guests from hand, current activity, or discard to the bottom of their decks. It remains an activity tile on both sides and never becomes an ongoing dismissal tile.
answers.evidence: Other base activity tiles → West Terrace paragraph.

answers.answer: There is no maximum hand or personal discard size. Gentry in your discard pile still belong to you and score normally; passing returns discarded gentry to hand.
answers.evidence: Gentry, screening, dismissal and family.

answers.answer: You may inspect all Reserve tiles and buy any one, including a tile underneath another in a stack; you are not restricted to the top tile. Every Reserve tile is public and available for selection.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve → Open Reserve.

answers.answer: You are not required to host whenever able; you may choose to pass. If required gentry or servants are unavailable for the chosen activity, choose another legal activity or pass; if no activity is possible, you must pass.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: choose host or pass; Hosting steps 4–5.

answers.answer: Yes. On a passing turn you may take the free refresh benefit, use one paid special-action Market refresh (if you have sufficient reputation and are above minimum), and use multiple Market Refresh VP cards, each for a separate full refresh. The once-per-turn limit applies only to the special-action Refresh Market; free pass refreshes and VP-card refreshes do not use that allowance. Follow the purchase-timing restriction: after buying on a Market Purchase/Builders’ Holiday benefit, you cannot refresh between purchases.
answers.evidence: Actions → special action limits and refresh methods; Builders’ Holiday / Market Purchase VP card.
